claim: For EC2, Compute Savings Plans give up to 66% off and EC2 Instance Savings Plans give up to 72% off, in exchange for a commitment to an amount of compute usage in $/hour for a one or three-year period.
question: What maximum discounts do Compute Savings Plans and EC2 Instance Savings Plans give compared with On-Demand?

values.spoken: Compute Savings Plans, up to sixty-six percent off

values.display: Amazon EC2 Instance Savings Plans (up to 72% off)
values.spoken: EC2 Instance Savings Plans, up to seventy-two percent off

qualifiers.scope: per Savings Plan type, compared with On-Demand prices
qualifiers.condition: commitment measured in $/hour for a one or three-year period

evidence.quote: There are four Savings Plan types: Compute Savings Plans (up to 66% off), Amazon EC2 Instance Savings Plans (up to 72% off), [Database Savings Plans](https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/database-pricing/) (up to 35% off for Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, and more), and [SageMaker AI Savings Plans](https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/ml-pricing/) (up to 64% off).

**[Savings Plans](https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/compute-pricing/)** are a flexible pricing model that offers significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to a specific amount of compute usage (measured in $/hour) for a one or three-year period.

note: Chapter 41 (namespace savingsplans) owns Savings Plans; this fact serves the EC2 purchasing comparison.

claim: Compute Savings Plans apply to any EC2 instance usage regardless of Region, instance family, operating system or tenancy and also cover Fargate and Lambda, while EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply to one instance family in one Region for a higher discount.
question: How does the scope of a Compute Savings Plan differ from an EC2 Instance Savings Plan?

values.display: regardless of Region, instance family, operating system, or tenancy
values.spoken: Compute Savings Plans follow you across Regions and families

values.display: a specific instance family within a Region
values.spoken: EC2 Instance Savings Plans fix one family in one Region

evidence.quote: Savings Plans relevant to Amazon EC2 come in two varieties: Compute Savings Plans automatically apply to any Amazon EC2 instance usage regardless of Region, instance family, operating system, or tenancy, and also cover Fargate and Lambda usage. Amazon EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply to a specific instance family within a Region, offering higher discounts in exchange for a more targeted commitment.

values.spoken: new families may have no Reserved Instance pricing

note: Decision guide last updated June 22, 2026; exam questions still test Reserved Instances.

values.spoken: the EBS volume is not single-tenant

claim: A VPC has a tenancy of default or dedicated; by default VPCs have default tenancy, and all instances in a VPC with dedicated tenancy run as Dedicated Instances.
question: What is the default tenancy of a VPC, and what happens to instances in a dedicated-tenancy VPC?

values.spoken: VPCs have default tenancy unless you choose dedicated

values.display: all instances in the VPC run as Dedicated Instances
values.spoken: a dedicated VPC makes every instance dedicated

evidence.quote: A VPC can have a tenancy of either `default` or `dedicated`. By default, your VPCs have `default` tenancy and instances launched into a `default` tenancy VPC have `default` tenancy.
Create a VPC with a tenancy of `dedicated`, so that all instances in the VPC run as Dedicated Instances.

claim: A Reserved Instance with default tenancy applies only to running instances with default tenancy, not to instances with dedicated tenancy, and the tenancy of a Reserved Instance cannot be changed through modification.
question: Does a default-tenancy Reserved Instance discount a Dedicated Instance?

values.display: it does not apply to a running instance with `dedicated` tenancy
values.spoken: default-tenancy Reserved Instances do not cover dedicated instances

values.display: can't use the modification process to change the tenancy
values.spoken: you cannot modify the tenancy of a Reserved Instance

qualifiers.condition: a Convertible Reserved Instance can be exchanged for one with a different tenancy

evidence.quote: When you purchase a Reserved Instance with default tenancy, it applies only to a running instance with `default` tenancy; it does not apply to a running instance with `dedicated` tenancy.

You can't use the modification process to change the tenancy of a Reserved Instance after you've purchased it. However, you can exchange a Convertible Reserved Instance for a new Convertible Reserved Instance with a different tenancy.

claim: There is no additional charge for the instance store volumes provided with an instance; they are included in the usage cost of the instance.
question: Do you pay separately for instance store volumes?

values.spoken: instance store is included in the instance price

qualifiers.condition: instance types that provide instance store volumes

evidence.quote: There is no additional charge to use the instance store volumes provided for your instance. Instance store volumes are included as part of the usage cost of the instance.

claim: Instance store is temporary block storage on disks physically attached to the host; its size and number of devices vary by instance type and size, and not every instance type provides instance store volumes.
question: Does every EC2 instance type include instance store, and what decides its size?

values.display: varies by instance type and instance size
values.spoken: it depends on the instance type and size

values.display: not every instance type provides instance store volumes
values.spoken: some types have no instance store

evidence.quote: An instance store consists of one or more instance store volumes exposed as block devices. The size of an instance store as well as the number of devices available varies by instance type and instance size. For example, not every instance type provides instance store volumes.
This storage is provided by disks that are physically attached to the host computer.

claim: Instance store volumes can be attached to an instance only when you launch it, not after launch.
question: Can you add an instance store volume to a running instance?

evidence.quote: Instance store volumes can be attached to an instance only when you launch it. You can't attach instance store volumes to an instance after you've launched it.

claim: When you stop an instance, the data on any instance store volumes is erased, so data you need must first be copied to persistent storage such as Amazon EBS or Amazon S3.
question: What happens to instance store data when an instance is stopped?

values.display: the data on any instance store volumes is erased
values.spoken: instance store data is erased on stop

evidence.quote: When you stop an instance, the data on any instance store volumes is erased. Before you stop an instance, verify that you've copied any data that you need from the instance store volumes to persistent storage, such as Amazon EBS or Amazon S3.

note: The reboot behaviour is in ec2-state-diff-instance-store-data.
